title: addition and subtraction of decimals to thousandths

lesson.title: Adding and Subtracting Decimals to Thousandths

steps.say: Hi friend, it's Ms. Yuanyuan! Imagine you're at school in Vancouver on a hot June day. Your water bottle has one point two five zero litres of water in it, and you top it up at the fountain with zero point three seven five more litres. How much water do you have now? To answer that, we need to add decimals — and today some of those decimals go all the way to thousandths.

First, let's meet a thousandth. In the number zero point three seven five, the three is three tenths, the seven is seven hundredths, and the five is five thousandths. A thousandth is what you get when one whole is cut into one thousand equal pieces — tiny! Each digit lives in its own place, and that place tells you its size.

Here's a picture that helps. Pretend one tiny cube is one thousandth. Then a rod of ten cubes is one hundredth, and a flat of one hundred cubes is one tenth. So zero point three seven five is three flats, seven rods, and five little cubes. See how the blocks and the digits match up perfectly?

Before we add anything, smart mathematicians make a guess. One point two five zero is close to one point three, and zero point three seven five is close to zero point four. One point three plus zero point four is one point seven. So our answer should land somewhere near one point seven. Now if we get something silly like seventeen, we'll know to check again.

Now the real adding. The golden rule is: line up the decimal points, so tenths sit under tenths, hundredths under hundredths, and thousandths under thousandths. Zero plus five is five thousandths. Five plus seven is twelve hundredths, so we write two and carry one. Two plus three plus that carried one is six tenths. One plus zero is one whole. The answer is one point six two five litres — right beside our guess of one point seven!

Subtracting works the same way. At the Granville Island market you buy a two kilogram bag of blueberries — that's two point zero zero zero kilograms. Your family uses zero point eight four five kilograms for muffins. Line up the dots and subtract. Since we can't take five from zero, we borrow across: two point zero zero zero minus zero point eight four five is one point one five five kilograms left. Check it: one point one five five plus zero point eight four five gives exactly two. It works!

One last trick for a tricky-looking one. Add zero point six and zero point four seven five. They look like different sizes, but zero point six is the same as zero point six zero zero — writing extra zeros on the end never changes a decimal's value, it just fills the empty places. Now add: five thousandths, seven plus zero is seven hundredths, six plus four is ten tenths, which becomes one whole. The answer is one point zero seven five.

So remember, my friend: with decimals you never line up the ends of the numbers — you line up the decimal points. Fill the empty spots with zeros, estimate first, then add or subtract just like whole numbers. You've got this!

lesson.answer: Line up the decimal points, fill empty places with zeros, then add or subtract just like whole numbers.

practice.question: Maya bikes 2.450 km along the Stanley Park seawall, then 1.875 km more to the beach. (a) How far did she bike altogether? (b) How much less is that than 5 km?
